pages.hook: A phone call in English follows a small script. If you know the first sentences, you can speak with confidence even when you cannot see the other person.

facts.label: Emergency number
facts.sub: Call 911 for police, fire or an ambulance in the USA.

facts.label: Country code
facts.sub: The USA calling code is +1. Brazil is +55.

facts.label: Phone numbers
facts.sub: Area code + 7 digits, like (503) 555-0123.

facts.label: Say who you are
facts.sub: On the phone say “This is Raj”, not “I am Raj”.

pages.polite: Say **Hi, is Raj there?** and **Who is this?** with a friendly voice. At the end, say **Thanks, bye!**

mythfact.s: In the USA you call 911 in an emergency.
On the phone, you say “I am Raj” to introduce yourself.
A US phone number has 10 digits with the area code.
Brazil’s country code is +1.
“Hold on” means “wait a moment”.
mythfact.why: You say it when you need a second.

lines: “Hi, this is Raj.
I can’t answer the phone right now.
Please leave a message and I’ll call you back later.”

decode.q: What should you do after the greeting?

lines: Sorry, I’m in a meeting.
Can I call you back at 5?
Thanks!

compare.br: In Brazil people answer “Alô?” and often ask “Quem fala?”. The emergency numbers are 190, 192 and 193.
compare.us: In the USA people answer “Hello?” and often say “Who’s this?” or “This is…”. The emergency number is 911.
compare.tip: Practice three phrases: “Is … there?”, “This is …” and “Can I call you back?”
compare.ask: Role-play: call a friend and say who you are. Do it out loud in English.

quiz.q: You call Raj. He answers. You want to know if it is him. You say…
quiz.why: Is … there? is the natural phone question.

quiz.q: You want to say who you are on the phone. You say…
The connection is bad. You say…
quiz.why: You’re breaking up = the signal is bad.

Reading quest — A call from the neighbor · part 1
text: My name is Raj, and I live in **San Jose**. Yesterday I was at home when my phone rang. I did not know the number. I said, “**Hello?**”
A man said, “**Hi, is Raj there?**” “**This is Raj**,” I said. “**Who is this?**” He answered, “It’s your neighbor from 4B. I forgot my key. Can you open the door?” “Sure,” I said. “I’m coming now.”

The call was not easy. The man was outside, and the signal was bad. “**You’re breaking up**,” I said. “**Hold on**.” I went to the window. Now I could hear him. He smiled and took a quick selfie with me at the door, a funny photo for his family.

opts: A phone call from a neighbor
fast.why: The neighbor calls because he forgot his key.

scan.q: What city does Raj live in?

tf.s: Raj knows the number at first.
The neighbor lives in 4B.
The signal is good during the whole call.
Raj opens the door.

order: The neighbor says he forgot his key.
The signal is bad and Raj goes to the window.

ctx.why: A phone rings when someone calls.
The signal is the connection of a phone.
Hold on = wait.

pages.think: How do you answer the phone in your language? How would you answer in English?

pages.title: Reading quest — A call from the neighbor · part 2
text: A British series called “Black Mirror” shows the dark side of phones. In real life, a phone can be very helpful. You **make a call**, you **take a selfie**, or you **hold the phone up** to find a better signal. If you **lose signal**, just go to the window.
The neighbor said, “Thanks, you’re the best!” “**Anytime**,” I said. “**Call me back** later!” And now we are good friends.

speed.q: Complete a fala: “Hey! ____?” (E aí! O que está rolando?)
speed.why: “What's going on” = O que está rolando

speed.q: Complete a fala: “____. Hold on.” (Está falhando. Espera aí.)
speed.why: “You're breaking up” = Está cortando

speed.q: Complete a fala: “You're breaking up. ____.” (Está falhando. Espera aí.)
speed.why: “Hold on” = Espera aí

speed.q: Complete a fala: “____ later!” (Me liga de volta depois!)

dict.say: Oh, hi! How can I help you?

errors.why: On the phone, we say This is + name.
Who is this? is the usual phone question.

errors.wrong: I make a call to you later.
errors.alt: I will to call you later.
errors.why: Use will + base verb for a promise.
Forget is irregular: forgot.

errors.wrong: Can you open me the door?
errors.alt: Can you open the door for I?
errors.why: Do not add me after open.

pages.title: Boss mission — Hello, who is this?

brief.teacher: You are Victor. Change the plan during the scene.
brief.student: You call your neighbor Raj. Victor answers the phone. Be clear and polite. You are the customer / visitor.

orders: I need to make a call.
complications: The other person did not hear you: repeat.

pages.title: Free production
pages.prompt: Você está no parque. Diga vamos tirar uma foto, que precisa fazer uma ligação e que não há sinal. Ligue à referência Black Mirror: mostra celulares e câmeras: take a photo, make a call.
pages.model: Let’s take a photo. I need to make a call. There is no signal. Black Mirror helps here.

tasks.name: Say it
tasks.model: I need to make a call.

items: Write a short voicemail greeting in English.
Listen to the dialogue again and shadow Victor.
Review: Hold on. / You’re breaking up. / Call me back.
